title: The Smart Way to Start Small and Still Win Big
channel: Chris Koerner on The Koerner Office Podcast

speakers.name: Dan
speakers.role: guest, owner of Apex Softwash, 10X Fitness gyms, Bluefield Builders and a roofing company (NE Pennsylvania)

idea.name: Gym in a small market that out-competes run-down local gyms
idea.one_liner: Open 24/7 gyms only in markets where existing gyms are poorly run, steal members with tactics like free 'show your ID Sundays', and use cheap wrapped trailers and community naming for local marketing

key_quotes.quote: So if you showed your ID from any other gym in the area on a Sunday, you could work at our gym for free.
So, I like to go into these markets where I know the gym's already there and I know that we could beat them.
So if you have any skills whatsoever and you can go out and see something happen in another part of the country, you can just bring it back here and it usually works.

claims.claim: Competitor closed on Sundays went out of business within a month of the free-Sunday promo
claims.quote: And within a month, that guy was out of business.
He has two gyms. He's opening his third.

acquisition_channels.details: wrapped trailer parked out front as billboard (~$5K vs $40K truck)
local Facebook group posts, crowd-sourced gym naming (~200 responses)
word of mouth in gym communities

ideas.delivery: 24/7 access gym run by a strong location manager

idea.name: Laundromat at an intersection with run-down competitors
idea.one_liner: Open a modern laundromat only at intersections that already have 2-4 old, run-down laundromats, capturing existing local behaviour

key_quotes.quote: I interviewed a guy, episode 58, that opens laundromats, and he will only open at an intersection that already has two to four other laundromats, assuming that they're garbage

claims.claim: He always captures the majority of the market
claims.quote: And he always always steals the majority of the market.

idea.name: Bitcoin miner reseller via Facebook Marketplace
idea.one_liner: Sell Bitcoin mining hardware through organic Facebook Marketplace posts across multiple accounts, funnelling leads to one place

key_quotes.quote: And so I had a company that did 9.8 million its first 90 days selling Bitcoin miners.
And so we created multiple accounts out of necessity and funneled all the leads back to one place.

claims.claim: $9.8M revenue in first 90 days, 100% organic Facebook Marketplace
claims.quote: And it was 100% through face organic Facebook marketplace posts.

acquisition_channels.details: organic Facebook Marketplace posts from multiple accounts

idea.name: Fencing company fed by Facebook Marketplace
idea.one_liner: Fencing installer getting all business from weekly organic Facebook Marketplace posts

key_quotes.quote: He gets 100% of his business from Facebook Marketplace.

claims.claim: $2.5M/yr, double-digit margins, posting about once a week
claims.quote: $2 and half million dollars a year, double- digit margins.

idea.name: Agency running Facebook accounts to recommend clients
idea.one_liner: Agency that operates multiple Facebook accounts to post listings and recommend local businesses in community groups (morally questioned by the speakers)

key_quotes.quote: There needs to be there needs to be an agency because I thought about that.
but if you have eight people recommend the same company it's like wow that really built trust and built value but

uk_legal_risk.reason: Fake recommendations/reviews are banned under the DMCC Act 2024 unfair practices rules and CPRs

ideas.other_uk_rules: Breaches Meta terms on fake accounts

idea.name: Single-court backyard pickleball club
idea.one_liner: Convert a 2,100 sq ft metal shop into a members-only pickleball court with key-fob access and cameras; validate demand with Facebook lead ads before spending $30-40K on build-out

key_quotes.quote: If I do all this, spend 30 to 40 grand, do marketing, put in a key fob, cameras, and all that, I can make 20 grand a month from it.
Cuz on paper, there's about 10,000 people within 10 miles of me that play pickle ball weekly.
And so it's going to cost me like 20 to 100 bucks to convert a$1,000 customer, $2,000 customer, which is amazing.

claims.claim: Leads converting under $2 each, 20-something leads in two days
claims.quote: Well, I just started this two days ago and I've got like 20 something leads.

claims.claim: Projected $20K/month at 100-200 members vs $2,500 renting to a home service business
claims.quote: So basically at where it stands today, I can rent the thing out for 2500 bucks to a home service business.

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook instant forms, Messenger ads and Typeform link with price, address and qualifiers

ideas.delivery: unstaffed court with key fob, cameras, cleaning service; pre-orders before build

stated_problem.quote: Like we don't have enough leads.
stated_problem.speaker: Dan

idea.name: Soft wash / power washing company
idea.one_liner: Residential and commercial soft washing grown past one truck through yard-sign discipline, bag-of-rock flyers aimed at the cleanest houses, a mission statement and VA-handled invoicing

key_quotes.quote: Like that yard sign is that freaking important like that.
You want to get a rock flyer.
Like your your c your customer is not the dirtiest house on the street.
I see no reason why like someone can't come in and like every week I have a virtual assistant come through on Friday, look at the jobs, send them out, and have those done.

claims.claim: About three crews gets a power washing company to $1M
claims.quote: It's you're probably doing like three crews gets you to a million.

claims.claim: 13 years in the business; considers it the most overrated home service due to TikTok
claims.quote: I'm like I've been doing for 13 years.

acquisition_channels.details: yard signs at every job, bagged-rock flyers in target neighbourhoods, trailer wraps

ideas.delivery: crews on F-550 trucks; VA does weekly invoicing; assistant handles mail; outsourced bookkeeping
ideas.other_uk_rules: Wastewater runoff from soft washing chemicals must not enter surface drains (Environment Agency)

idea.name: Marketing-only roofing company
idea.one_liner: Roofing company that owns no trucks, only does marketing and sales, and subcontracts all installation work

key_quotes.quote: Technically, you know, to go one level, my roofing company, like we don't have a truck, you know, like we only have the phone because we're just marketing, right?

idea.name: Buy an HVAC business
idea.one_liner: Rather than starting from zero, buy an existing licensed HVAC company: a necessity service with more leads than capacity and licensing barriers

key_quotes.quote: If it was going to be a service business, it would probably have to be HVAC and he like you just need those two things.
I wouldn't get my HVAC license.
HVAC has so many leads. They don't have enough work.

ideas.other_uk_rules: Gas Safe registration and F-gas certification needed for heating/AC work

idea.name: Buy adjacent strip mall via a goodwill letter
idea.one_liner: Acquire neighbouring commercial property by leaving the elderly owner a letter to keep on file, connecting your own parcels

key_quotes.quote: If you're ever, you know, in the point where you want to sell this thing, like keep this letter in your file and like call me and go Birds." Because I knew he's a big Eagles fan.
So, I had some a friend of mine already offered to just add 50 grand to the contract to buy it.

idea.name: Five-star-review-driven window cleaning company
idea.one_liner: Window cleaning/power washing company where pay and mission are tied to getting a five-star review, with prepaid review postcards

key_quotes.quote: unbeliev like like their pay everything was based on the five star review and it was really really cool because it was like such a tangible metric like did you

acquisition_channels.details: five-star reviews and Google Business Profile

ideas.other_uk_rules: Incentivised reviews must be disclosed (CMA / DMCC Act)
